{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793107484551,"sessionID":"ses_e8278f9daffeVCxJO0V1W0MLgk","part":{"id":"prt_17d872344001EdLPcy2xjH3Kw5","messageID":"msg_17d871f890018RruM0iud1LJ5S","sessionID":"ses_e8278f9daffeVCxJO0V1W0MLgk","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm working through a left-looking Cholesky algorithm processed row by row, where each diagonal entry becomes a square root of an accumulated sum and each off-diagonal entry gets divided by the corresponding diagonal value.\n\nThis reveals a sequential dependency across j within each row, since each column depends on earlier columns in the same row via forward substitution, while the dot products themselves can still be parallelized. And across rows, row i requires fully finalized values from all rows j<i, so rows form an inherent dependency chain that resists parallelization.\n\nThat leads me to the column-oriented approach instead: for each column j, compute the diagonal element first, then update all rows i>j in parallel using dot products over the first j elements. This preserves identical summation order to the sequential version, so floating-point results should match exactly as long as the compiler doesn't contract multiply-adds into FMA instructions, which depends on build flags and whether -march=native enables FMA on the target CPU.\n\nSince nvcc also applies FMA contraction by default on GPU, exact bitwise matching between CPU and GPU isn't realistic, and I shouldn't worry about it given the 1e-6 relative tolerance — I'll just preserve the same ordering and accept minor rounding differences rather than trying to force non-FMA operations everywhere.\n\nI'm also noting that the matrix generation step (computing A = B*B^T) is its own O(n^3) operation separate from the timed Cholesky decomposition region, so I need to clarify whether parallelizing that generation step is actually required by the task.\n\nI'll keep things manageable by putting the required decomposition kernel on GPU, and also moving the generation product and validation step onto GPU with simple kernels that preserve identical summation order, since those are also O(n^3) costs worth accelerating even though they aren't the timed region.\n\nFor the column-by-column Cholesky design, each column launches a kernel doing a sequential sum reduction for the diagonal element and then updates the remaining entries below it -- for n=512 that's hundreds of small launches, which should still run in just a few milliseconds total, and scales reasonably for larger n since each column's work grows with matrix size. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793107509248,"sessionID":"ses_e8278f9daffeVCxJO0V1W0MLgk","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_016cWENYaNXHVGrviYP3H4LB","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Parallel (CUDA) Cholesky decomposition (unblocked, column-oriented)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n//\n// Algorithm (same arithmetic and summation order as the sequential reference):\n//   for j = 0..n-1:\n//     L[j][j] = sqrt(A[j][j] - sum_{k<j} L[j][k]^2)\n//     for i = j+1..n-1 (in parallel):\n//       L[i][j] = (A[i][j] - sum_{k<j} L[i][k] * L[j][k]) / L[j][j]\n//\n// Column j depends only on columns < j, so each column is one kernel launch\n// whose rows are computed by independent threads. The diagonal value is\n// recomputed by every thread of the column (it is a cheap, identical\n// computation) so no extra synchronization or launch is required.\n//\n// Device layout: the working matrix M is column-major with respect to L,\n// i.e. L[r][c] lives at M[c*n + r]. This makes the per-row accesses of a\n// column step coalesced across threads.\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                   \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr unsigned kColumnBlock = 256;\nconstexpr unsigned kTileDim = 32;\nconstexpr unsigned kGramBlock = 16;\n\n// RAII wrapper for device memory\ntemplate <typename T>\nclass DeviceBuffer {\npublic:\n    explicit DeviceBuffer(size_t count) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&ptr_), count * sizeof(T)));\n    }\n    ~DeviceBuffer() {\n        if (ptr_) cudaFree(ptr_);\n    }\n    DeviceBuffer(const DeviceBuffer&) = delete;\n    DeviceBuffer& operator=(const DeviceBuffer&) = delete;\n\n    T* get() const { return ptr_; }\n\nprivate:\n    T* ptr_ = nullptr;\n};\n\n// One column step of the factorization. Thread for row i (i >= j) computes\n// L[i][j]; the thread with i == j produces the diagonal entry L[j][j].\n__global__ void choleskyColumnKernel(double* __restrict__ M,\n                                     double* __restrict__ diag,\n                                     int* __restrict__ firstFail,\n                                     size_t n, size_t j) {\n    const size_t i = j + static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (i >= n) return;\n\n    // L[j][j] = sqrt(A[j][j] - sum_{k<j} L[j][k]^2). A[j][j] is still the\n    // original value here: M[j*n + j] is only ever written via diag[].\n    double dsum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n        const double ljk = M[k * n + j];\n        dsum += ljk * ljk;\n    }\n    const double val = M[j * n + j] - dsum;\n    const double d = sqrt(val);\n\n    if (i == j) {\n        diag[j] = d;\n        if (val <= 0.0) {\n            atomicMin(firstFail, static_cast<int>(j));\n        }\n        return;\n    }\n\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n        sum += M[k * n + i] * M[k * n + j];\n    }\n    M[j * n + i] = (M[j * n + i] - sum) / d;\n}\n\n// Tiled transpose: out(r, c) = in(c, r).\n// When kLowerOnly is set, the output is the lower-triangular factor: the\n// strict upper part is zeroed and the diagonal is taken from diag[].\ntemplate <bool kLowerOnly>\n__global__ void transposeKernel(const double* __restrict__ in,\n                                double* __restrict__ out,\n                                const double* __restrict__ diag,\n                                size_t n) {\n    __shared__ double tile[kTileDim][kTileDim + 1];\n\n    const size_t x = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * kTileDim + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t y = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * kTileDim + threadIdx.y;\n    if (x < n && y < n) {\n        tile[threadIdx.y][threadIdx.x] = in[y * n + x];\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    // Output element (r, c) = (blockIdx.x*T + ty, blockIdx.y*T + tx)\n    const size_t c = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * kTileDim + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * kTileDim + threadIdx.y;\n    if (c < n && r < n) {\n        double v = tile[threadIdx.x][threadIdx.y];\n        if constexpr (kLowerOnly) {\n            if (c > r) {\n                v = 0.0;\n            } else if (c == r) {\n                v = diag[r];\n            }\n        }\n        out[r * n + c] = v;\n    }\n}\n\n// Gram product: Y = X * X^T (row-major), i.e. Y[i][j] = sum_k X[i][k] * X[j][k]\n__global__ void gramKernel(const double* __restrict__ X, double* __restrict__ Y, size_t n) {\n    const size_t j = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * kGramBlock + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * kGramBlock + threadIdx.y;\n    if (i >= n || j >= n) return;\n\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n        sum += X[i * n + k] * X[j * n + k];\n    }\n    Y[i * n + j] = sum;\n}\n\n// Y = X * X^T computed on the GPU (row-major n x n matrices)\nvoid gramProduct(const std::vector<double>& X, std::vector<double>& Y, const size_t n) {\n    if (n == 0) return;\n    DeviceBuffer<double> dX(n * n);\n    DeviceBuffer<double> dY(n * n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dX.get(), X.data(), n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    const dim3 block(kGramBlock, kGramBlock);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned>((n + kGramBlock - 1) / kGramBlock),\n                    static_cast<unsigned>((n + kGramBlock - 1) / kGramBlock));\n    gramKernel<<<grid, block>>>(dX.get(), dY.get(), n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(Y.data(), dY.get(), n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order; on success it holds L (row-major, zero upper part)\n    if (n == 0) return true;\n\n    const size_t nn = n * n;\n    DeviceBuffer<double> dA(nn);     // row-major input, later reused for row-major output\n    DeviceBuffer<double> dM(nn);     // column-major working copy of L\n    DeviceBuffer<double> dDiag(n);   // diagonal of L\n    DeviceBuffer<int> dFail(1);      // smallest failing diagonal index (n if none)\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dA.get(), A.data(), nn * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    const int noFailure = static_cast<int>(n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dFail.get(), &noFailure, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    const dim3 tBlock(kTileDim, kTileDim);\n    const dim3 tGrid(static_cast<unsigned>((n + kTileDim - 1) / kTileDim),\n                     static_cast<unsigned>((n + kTileDim - 1) / kTileDim));\n\n    // dM = A^T (column-major view of A)\n    transposeKernel<false><<<tGrid, tBlock>>>(dA.get(), dM.get(), nullptr, n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        const size_t rows = n - j;\n        const unsigned grid = static_cast<unsigned>((rows + kColumnBlock - 1) / kColumnBlock);\n        choleskyColumnKernel<<<grid, kColumnBlock>>>(dM.get(), dDiag.get(), dFail.get(), n, j);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    }\n\n    // dA = L (row-major, upper part zeroed)\n    transposeKernel<true><<<tGrid, tBlock>>>(dM.get(), dA.get(), dDiag.get(), n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    int failIdx = noFailure;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(&failIdx, dFail.get(), sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n    if (failIdx < static_cast<int>(n)) {\n        printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\",\n               static_cast<size_t>(failIdx));\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(A.data(), dA.get(), nn * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Compute A = B * B^T on the GPU\n    gramProduct(B, A, n);\n\n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n\n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n\n    // Compute L * L^T on the GPU\n    gramProduct(L, reconstructed, n);\n\n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n\n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n\n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n// Select the GPU and create the CUDA context up front so that context setup\n// is not included in the timed decomposition.\nvoid initCuda() {\n    int deviceCount = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&deviceCount));\n    if (deviceCount == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"No CUDA-capable device found\\n\");\n        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(0));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(nullptr));\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    initCuda();\n\n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n\n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n\n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n\n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","time":{"start":1793107509154,"end":1793107509220}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17d8904fd001cvu1c4Wv6NGWin","sessionID":"ses_e8278f9daffeVCxJO0V1W0MLgk","messageID":"msg_17d88f41c001uWGuufWTNy2PjR"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793107574575,"sessionID":"ses_e8278f9daffeVCxJO0V1W0MLgk","part":{"id":"prt_17d89d9e50016ZNc0ZQmoLoc27","messageID":"msg_17d89d52f001xzixhYSYyTOK8O","sessionID":"ses_e8278f9daffeVCxJO0V1W0MLgk","type":"reasoning","text":"It's passing but the speedup is marginal at n=512 since launch overhead and redundant loops dominate. At n=2048 it's much faster than baseline, so the gains show up at scale. I'm digging into why the per-column kernel is slow at small n—each thread's serial dot-product loop with global memory loads creates a latency chain.\n\nI'm considering staging shared rows into shared memory to avoid redundant global loads, since each thread currently redundantly reads the same diagonal row data. The tricky part is sizing shared memory correctly for larger n without hitting the 48KB limit.\n\nBefore optimizing further, I should actually measure where time goes—checking if nsys profiling is available, or just comparing timing numbers against expected launch overhead to see if the 50us per launch for n=512 is reasonable or a sign of inefficiency.\n\nConfirming it's latency-bound: with small n, one block per column means low occupancy, and the serial dot-product loop issues dependent loads with unknown trip counts that the compiler can't easily unroll. Adding manual unrolling (like `#pragma unroll 4`) should help overlap those loads without changing the sequential sum order, but the deeper fix is recognizing that within a column step, the (n-j) dot products are independent and could be parallelized across more threads/blocks rather than relying on compiler unrolling alone.\n\nWith limited threads we're latency bound regardless, so splitting the dot product across threads with a block reduction becomes a reasonable parallelization strategy, even though it changes summation order slightly. Since the correctness requirement allows 1e-6 relative tolerance rather than bit-identical results, this tradeoff toward parallelism over strict sequential summation seems acceptable.\n\nI'm checking whether the hash actually matches the original though - comparing the two hashes shows they differ, with the minimum value differing in low-order digits, which suggests the mismatch traces back further than my reduction choice. It looks like this divergence may originate from the generation step itself, since GPU and CPU FMA contraction behavior for the gram product computation could differ, meaning the underlying matrix A is already slightly different before my changes even come into play, so chasing bitwise parity with the original seems less productive than ensuring internal consistency.\n\nI'll leave that rounding-vs-contraction check aside for now and focus on performance instead. Estimating the sequential-order dot product's minimum cycle cost, I figure something like 2-3ms should be achievable with shared memory staging versus the current 25ms, while preserving exact summation order — about a 10x speedup. I'm now sketching a v2 kernel design: 256-thread blocks iterating over rows, with a shared memory tile caching chunks of the pivot row so threads can cooperatively load and reuse that data for both the running sum and dot product computations.\n\nContinuing the kernel logic, I realize dsum and dot can be computed in the same chunked loop since both accumulate over increasing k, preserving the original order. I'm working out the per-thread accumulator logic for diag and dot terms, handling the i==j edge case, and finalizing with the sqrt and division steps to update the matrix column — checking that the summation order matches the original exactly.\n\nWriting kernel setup...\n\nStill writing kernel logic...\n\nChecking that each thread's dsum stays consistent since they all iterate the same row values in order, so there's no divergence risk there. A[j][j] is still the\n    // original value here: M[j*n + j] is only ever written via diag[].\n    double dsum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n        const double ljk = M[k * n + j];\n        dsum += ljk * ljk;\n    }\n    const double val = M[j * n + j] - dsum;\n    const double d = sqrt(val);\n\n    if (i == j) {\n        diag[j] = d;\n        if (val <= 0.0) {\n            atomicMin(firstFail, static_cast<int>(j));\n        }\n        return;\n    }\n\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n        sum += M[k * n + i] * M[k * n + j];\n    }\n    M[j * n + i] = (M[j * n + i] - sum) / d;\n}","newString":"// One column step of the factorization. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793107727061,"sessionID":"ses_e8278f9daffeVCxJO0V1W0MLgk","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_015pDaQYRtGWQXCMrPA1FFFq","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// CUDA-parallel Cholesky decomposition (unblocked, row-oriented)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n//\n// Algorithm:\n//   for j = 0..n-1:\n//     L[j][j] = sqrt(A[j][j] - sum_{k<j} L[j][k]^2)\n//     for i = j+1..n-1 (all rows in parallel):\n//       L[i][j] = (A[i][j] - sum_{k<j} L[i][k] * L[j][k]) / L[j][j]\n//\n// Column j depends only on columns < j, so each column is one kernel launch.\n// Within a launch, one warp handles one row i: the lanes split the k-sum and\n// the partial sums are combined with a warp shuffle reduction. The working\n// matrix is row-major, so the lanes read consecutive k values (coalesced).\n// The diagonal L[j][j] is recomputed by each warp from the same data (a cheap,\n// identical computation), so no extra launch or synchronization is needed.\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                   \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr unsigned kWarpSize = 32;\nconstexpr unsigned kWarpsPerBlock = 8;\nconstexpr unsigned kBlockThreads = kWarpSize * kWarpsPerBlock;\nconstexpr unsigned kGramBlock = 16;\nconstexpr unsigned kFinalizeBlock = 256;\n\n// RAII wrapper for device memory\ntemplate <typename T>\nclass DeviceBuffer {\npublic:\n    explicit DeviceBuffer(size_t count) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&ptr_), count * sizeof(T)));\n    }\n    ~DeviceBuffer() {\n        if (ptr_) cudaFree(ptr_);\n    }\n    DeviceBuffer(const DeviceBuffer&) = delete;\n    DeviceBuffer& operator=(const DeviceBuffer&) = delete;\n\n    T* get() const { return ptr_; }\n\nprivate:\n    T* ptr_ = nullptr;\n};\n\n__device__ __forceinline__ double warpReduceSum(double v) {\n    // Result is valid in lane 0\n    for (unsigned offset = kWarpSize / 2; offset > 0; offset >>= 1) {\n        v += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, v, offset);\n    }\n    return v;\n}\n\n// One column step of the factorization. Warp w of block b handles row\n// i = j + b*kWarpsPerBlock + w (i >= j). Row i of the working matrix W holds\n// A[i][*] on entry and L[i][*] (for columns < j) on exit.\n__global__ void choleskyColumnKernel(double* __restrict__ W,\n                                     double* __restrict__ diag,\n                                     int* __restrict__ firstFail,\n                                     size_t n, size_t j) {\n    const unsigned lane = threadIdx.x % kWarpSize;\n    const unsigned warp = threadIdx.x / kWarpSize;\n    const size_t i = j + static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * kWarpsPerBlock + warp;\n    if (i >= n) return;  // warp-uniform: whole warp exits together\n\n    const double* rowI = W + i * n;\n    const double* rowJ = W + j * n;\n\n    double dsum = 0.0;  // sum_{k<j} L[j][k]^2\n    double sum = 0.0;   // sum_{k<j} L[i][k] * L[j][k]\n    #pragma unroll 4\n    for (size_t k = lane; k < j; k += kWarpSize) {\n        const double ljk = rowJ[k];\n        dsum += ljk * ljk;\n        sum += rowI[k] * ljk;\n    }\n    dsum = warpReduceSum(dsum);\n    sum = warpReduceSum(sum);\n    // Broadcast so every lane holds the identical values\n    dsum = __shfl_sync(0xffffffffu, dsum, 0);\n    sum = __shfl_sync(0xffffffffu, sum, 0);\n\n    // L[j][j] = sqrt(A[j][j] - sum_{k<j} L[j][k]^2). A[j][j] is still the\n    // original value: W[j][j] is never written during the factorization.\n    const double val = W[j * n + j] - dsum;\n    const double d = sqrt(val);\n\n    if (lane != 0) return;\n    if (i == j) {\n        diag[j] = d;\n        if (val <= 0.0) {\n            atomicMin(firstFail, static_cast<int>(j));\n        }\n        return;\n    }\n\n    W[i * n + j] = (W[i * n + j] - sum) / d;\n}\n\n// Final pass: zero the strict upper triangle and place the diagonal.\n__global__ void finalizeKernel(double* __restrict__ W, const double* __restrict__ diag, size_t n) {\n    const size_t idx = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (idx >= n * n) return;\n    const size_t r = idx / n;\n    const size_t c = idx % n;\n    if (c > r) {\n        W[idx] = 0.0;\n    } else if (c == r) {\n        W[idx] = diag[r];\n    }\n}\n\n// Gram product: Y = X * X^T (row-major), i.e. Y[i][j] = sum_k X[i][k] * X[j][k]\n__global__ void gramKernel(const double* __restrict__ X, double* __restrict__ Y, size_t n) {\n    const size_t j = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * kGramBlock + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * kGramBlock + threadIdx.y;\n    if (i >= n || j >= n) return;\n\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n        sum += X[i * n + k] * X[j * n + k];\n    }\n    Y[i * n + j] = sum;\n}\n\n// Y = X * X^T computed on the GPU (row-major n x n matrices)\nvoid gramProduct(const std::vector<double>& X, std::vector<double>& Y, const size_t n) {\n    if (n == 0) return;\n    DeviceBuffer<double> dX(n * n);\n    DeviceBuffer<double> dY(n * n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dX.get(), X.data(), n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    const dim3 block(kGramBlock, kGramBlock);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned>((n + kGramBlock - 1) / kGramBlock),\n                    static_cast<unsigned>((n + kGramBlock - 1) / kGramBlock));\n    gramKernel<<<grid, block>>>(dX.get(), dY.get(), n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(Y.data(), dY.get(), n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order; on success it holds L (row-major, zero upper part)\n    if (n == 0) return true;\n\n    const size_t nn = n * n;\n    DeviceBuffer<double> dW(nn);     // row-major working matrix\n    DeviceBuffer<double> dDiag(n);   // diagonal of L\n    DeviceBuffer<int> dFail(1);      // smallest failing diagonal index (n if none)\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dW.get(), A.data(), nn * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    const int noFailure = static_cast<int>(n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dFail.get(), &noFailure, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        const size_t rows = n - j;\n        const unsigned grid = static_cast<unsigned>((rows + kWarpsPerBlock - 1) / kWarpsPerBlock);\n        choleskyColumnKernel<<<grid, kBlockThreads>>>(dW.get(), dDiag.get(), dFail.get(), n, j);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    }\n\n    finalizeKernel<<<static_cast<unsigned>((nn + kFinalizeBlock - 1) / kFinalizeBlock),\n                     kFinalizeBlock>>>(dW.get(), dDiag.get(), n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    int failIdx = noFailure;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(&failIdx, dFail.get(), sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n    if (failIdx < static_cast<int>(n)) {\n        printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\",\n               static_cast<size_t>(failIdx));\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(A.data(), dW.get(), nn * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Compute A = B * B^T on the GPU\n    gramProduct(B, A, n);\n\n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n\n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n\n    // Compute L * L^T on the GPU\n    gramProduct(L, reconstructed, n);\n\n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n\n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n\n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n// Select the GPU and create the CUDA context up front so that context setup\n// is not included in the timed decomposition.\nvoid initCuda() {\n    int deviceCount = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&deviceCount));\n    if (deviceCount == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"No CUDA-capable device found\\n\");\n        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(0));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(nullptr));\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    initCuda();\n\n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n\n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n\n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n\n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","time":{"start":1793107727011,"end":1793107727032}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17d8c55b00013mMRHwHOUdhF6y","sessionID":"ses_e8278f9daffeVCxJO0V1W0MLgk","messageID":"msg_17d8c51cd001FZnsIRVxNEt2nd"}}
